Future Clips — style system

One niche does not get one look

The reference library runs the same niche several different ways — fitness as a whitepaper, as a phone photo, as an illustrated character — and all of them work, because they are aimed at different readers. So the engine now carries 8 styles, and a niche gets a ranked list rather than an answer.

The styles

Each one is built to a specific set in the local reference library, not invented. A style is a renderer over the same campaign JSON — the content model does not change when the look does.

Native9:16

Full-bleed phone photography with a heavy stroked caption. Looks like a post, not an ad — the format the gym niche actually runs.

fitness · gym · lifestyle · nutrition

Mascot9:16

Brand-colour grounds with a supplied mascot and speech bubbles. Needs one mascot asset; reuses it across every slide.

fitness · supplements · gaming · creator

Bedrock4:5

Cream ground, badge lockup, black-over-accent headline and a cel-shaded character. Needs a generated character sheet.

fitness · gym · calisthenics · supplements

Clinical4:5

Whitepaper grammar — serif headline, small body, labelled diagrams, a named source. Reads as evidence, not a pitch.

health · longevity · fitness · supplements

Editorial4:5

Near-white, airy serif with a single italic accent word, small body copy, a desaturated figure low in frame.

mindset · running · wellness · self-improvement

Document4:5

Numbered sections, real tables with measured columns, worked examples and a footnote. For content whose value is the specifics.

finance · personal finance · business · legal

Poster4:5

Black ground, condensed display type set to span the measure, one accent word, a script aside and a numbered chip.

marketing · design · creator · social media

Pastel4:5

Warm cream ground, serif question headline, tinted body panels, numbered takeaways and a dashed save-this box.

finance · beauty · skincare · lifestyle

Every niche, every style rendered

Green is the style the niche usually runs. Orange is the same campaign pushed through a style it normally would not use — which is often the reason a set gets noticed.

How a niche gets its styles

Scoring is deliberately blunt, and it ranks rather than filters — every style stays reachable at the bottom of the list.

GET /api/styles?niche=skincare

  pastel     native    1080x1350   made for this niche
  editorial  adjacent  1080x1350   used by neighbouring niches
  native     adjacent  1080x1920
  clinical   stretch   1080x1350   unusual here, which is sometimes the point
  document   stretch   1080x1350
  mascot     stretch   1080x1920
  poster     stretch   1080x1350

The generated character

One style in the library cannot be built from stock photography: it needs the same illustrated figure in many poses. That one is now real, made with gpt-image-2 against a live key.

probe first, because gpt-image-2 shipped after the model's training cutoff

  returns        b64_json only, no url
  1024x1536      low 158 tok  $0.0047   9s
                 med 1372 tok $0.0412  19s
                 high 5488 tok $0.1646  67s
  1024x1792      accepted, closer to 9:16 AND cheaper than 1024x1536

consistency: draw every pose in ONE generation, then cut it up.
one image cannot drift from itself.

  3 sheets @ medium   $0.126
  4 poses cut         translucency 0.003 (limit 0.06) — all PASS
  every later render  $0.00

What broke building it

  • A cache that charged twiceThe generated-image cache put the caller's label in the filename, so the identical sheet requested by the CLI and by the studio missed each other's entry and was paid for twice. It is content-addressed now — the label is a ledger annotation, not identity. Cost $0.25 to find.
  • I reintroduced the bug the engine exists to preventTwo styles set a subline with bare text() at a fixed size instead of fitting it, and long copy ran straight off the frame. The fix was not just to fit it: hook.sub means a standfirst in one style and a one-line aside in another, so the kit now has an aside() that picks a size band from the copy length and wraps.
  • A chip sized by guessThe pastel score pill was a fixed 178px wide, so "the usual cause" rendered as "e usual caus". It now measures the label against the real face and sizes to it.
  • Fractional geometryLayout maths produces fractional heights; sharp demands integers. Rounding inside plate() fixed it for every style rather than at each call site.
  • An empty panelPastel drew its tinted body panel whether or not the campaign had body copy for it, leaving a blank pink block. It is gated on content now.
